    // The merge state after accepting every masked edge whose two endpoints AND
    // all their neighbours are still free. Entry v is -1 while vertex v is free,
    // -2 once it is blocked by a nearby collapse, and otherwise the vertex it has
    // been merged into — which for a collapse target is itself, so one array
    // records all three conditions.
    CollapseClaims(edges: Array<VertexPair>, neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>,
                   collapseMask: Array<Boolean>, vertexCount: Integer): Array<Integer>
        => edges.Count.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(Repeat(vertexCount, -1), (state, e) =>
            collapseMask[e]
                .And(HasFreeNeighborhood(state, neighbors, edges[e].A.Value))
                .And(HasFreeNeighborhood(state, neighbors, edges[e].B.Value))
                    ? ClaimedByCollapse(state, neighbors, edges[e])
                    : state);

    // The state with both endpoints of an accepted edge pointing at its A end, and
    // every other vertex of their two rings blocked for the rest of the pass.
    ClaimedByCollapse(state: Array<Integer>, neighbors: Array<Array<VertexIndex>>, edge: VertexPair): Array<Integer>
        => state.Count.MapRange(v =>
            (v == edge.A.Value).Or(v == edge.B.Value)
                ? edge.A.Value
                : (RowContains(neighbors[edge.A.Value], VertexIndex(v))
                    .Or(RowContains(neighbors[edge.B.Value], VertexIndex(v)))
                        ? -2
                        : state[v]));

    // True when edge e was accepted by `CollapseClaims`: its B end points at its A
    // end, and its A end points at itself.
    IsAcceptedCollapse(edges: Array<VertexPair>, state: Array<Integer>, e: Integer): Boolean
        => (edges[e].A.Value != edges[e].B.Value)
            .And(state[edges[e].A.Value] == edges[e].A.Value)
            .And(state[edges[e].B.Value] == edges[e].A.Value);

    // The positions after every accepted collapse has moved its surviving endpoint
    // to the point `placement` chooses for that edge.
    CollapsedPositions(positions: Array<Point3D>, edges: Array<VertexPair>, state: Array<Integer>,
                       placement: Function1<Integer, Point3D>): Array<Point3D>
        => edges.Count.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(positions, (moved, e) =>
            IsAcceptedCollapse(edges, state, e)
                ? moved.Count.MapRange(v => v == edges[e].A.Value ? placement(e) : moved[v])
                : moved);

    // The idempotent representative table a collapse state implies: an untouched
    // vertex represents itself, and everything else its merge target.
    CollapseRepresentatives(state: Array<Integer>): Array<VertexIndex>
        => state.Count.MapRange(v => VertexIndex(state[v] < 0 ? v : state[v]));

    // Every masked edge collapsed at once, subject to the link condition and the
    // adjacent-endpoint rule. `placement` gives the surviving position of each
    // collapsed edge, taking the edge number — the midpoint for a plain collapse,
    // the quadric minimizer for decimation.
    CollapseEdges(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, collapseMask: Array<Boolean>,
                  placement: Function1<Integer, Point3D>): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var neighbors = self.VertexNeighborTable(topology);
        var legal = topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e =>
            collapseMask[e].And(SatisfiesLinkCondition(topology, neighbors, e)));
        var state = CollapseClaims(topology.UndirectedEdges, neighbors, legal, self.Positions.Count);
        var moved = CollapsedPositions(self.Positions, topology.UndirectedEdges, state, placement);
        return self.ApplyRemap(CompactMerge(CollapseRepresentatives(state), i => moved[i]));
    }

    // True when collapsing an edge would drag a boundary vertex into the interior
    // or an interior vertex onto the boundary. Refusing those is what keeps an open
    // border where the author put it.
    CrossesBoundary(boundary: Array<Boolean>, pair: VertexPair): Boolean
        => boundary[pair.A.Value] != boundary[pair.B.Value];

    // One undirected edge collapsed to its midpoint. The single-operator form of
    // `CollapseEdges`.
    CollapseEdge(self: TriangleMesh3D, edge: UndirectedEdgeIndex): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        return self.CollapseEdges(topology, SingleEdgeMask(topology.EdgeCount, edge),
            e => self.EdgeMidpoint(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)));
    }

    // Every edge shorter than `minLength` collapsed to its midpoint, except those
    // that would cross the boundary. Only an independent set of them survives the
    // conflict rule, so short edges left over are collapsed by a later pass.
    CollapseShortEdges(self: TriangleMesh3D, minLength: Number): TriangleMesh3D
    {
        var topology = self.TopologyOf;
        var boundary = self.BoundaryVertexFlags(topology);
        return self.CollapseEdges(topology, topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e =>
            (self.EdgeLength(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)) < minLength)
                .And(CrossesBoundary(boundary, topology.UndirectedEdges[e]).Not)),
            e => self.EdgeMidpoint(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e)));
    }

    //==
    // # Edge flip
    //
    // Regularization. Flipping the shared edge of two triangles swaps which
    // diagonal of their quadrilateral is drawn, changing valence without moving a
    // single vertex — so a flip pass rewrites the face table and leaves the
    // position array alone, and the face COUNT is unchanged.
    //
    // A flip is legal only when the edge is interior AND the diagonal it would
    // draw is not already an edge: flipping onto an existing edge would leave two
    // faces sharing the same pair of vertices, which is not a manifold.
    //
    // The conflict rule claims VERTICES, not faces. Claiming faces is the obvious
    // rule and it is wrong: on an octahedron every equatorial edge sees the SAME
    // two poles, so two face-disjoint flips would each draw the pole-to-pole
    // diagonal and the second would land on the edge the first just made. Four
    // vertices per flip, claimed together, rules that out — and being stricter
    // costs nothing, because a rejected flip is simply reconsidered next pass.

    // True when the two vertices are already joined by an undirected edge.
    AreAdjacent(edges: Array<VertexPair>, a: VertexIndex, b: VertexIndex): Boolean
        => edges.Any(pair =>
            (pair.A.Value == a.Value).And(pair.B.Value == b.Value)
                .Or((pair.A.Value == b.Value).And(pair.B.Value == a.Value)));

    // The claim entry of a vertex, reading the "none" index as unclaimed. `And` is
    // an ordinary function and does not short-circuit, so a boundary edge's absent
    // far apex has to be kept off the subscript rather than guarded ahead of it.
    ClaimAt(claims: Array<Integer>, vertex: VertexIndex): Integer
        => vertex.IsNone ? -1 : claims[vertex.Value];

    // True when an edge could be flipped at all: interior, and its two apexes are
    // not already joined.
    IsFlipCandidate(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, e: Integer): Boolean
    {
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        return far.IsPresent.And(AreAdjacent(topology.UndirectedEdges, near, far).Not);
    }

    // The claim table after accepting every masked, flippable edge whose four
    // vertices are all still unclaimed. Entry v is -1 while vertex v is unclaimed,
    // and otherwise the number of the edge whose flip claimed it.
    FlipVertexClaims(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, flipMask: Array<Boolean>): Array<Integer>
        => topology.EdgeCount.MapRange(e => e).Reduce(Repeat(self.Positions.Count, -1), (claims, e) =>
            flipMask[e]
                .And(self.IsFlipCandidate(topology, e))
                .And(ClaimAt(claims, topology.UndirectedEdges[e].A) < 0)
                .And(ClaimAt(claims, topology.UndirectedEdges[e].B) < 0)
                .And(ClaimAt(claims, self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e))) < 0)
                .And(ClaimAt(claims, self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e))) < 0)
                    ? self.ClaimedByFlip(topology, claims, e)
                    : claims);

    // The claim table with all four vertices of an accepted flip marked.
    ClaimedByFlip(self: TriangleMesh3D, topology: TriangleMeshTopology, claims: Array<Integer>, e: Integer): Array<Integer>
    {
        var pair = topology.UndirectedEdges[e];
        var near = self.EdgeApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        var far = self.EdgeFarApex(topology, UndirectedEdgeIndex(e));
        return claims.Count.MapRange(v =>
            (v == pair.A.Value).Or(v == pair.B.Value).Or(v == near.Value).Or(v == far.Value)
                ? e
                : claims[v]);
    }
